samples.summary: Store-level merge refusal is silent — it bypasses the RangeOpRefusal/notice channel this same PR built for every other merge refusal
samples.evidence: `mergeSelection` now does `if (!(await this.store.setMerge(anchor, span))) return false;` with no `this.reportRefusal(...)`. The toolbar path (`view/spreadsheet.ts:563 toggleMergeCells`) only re-renders on `true` and shows nothing on `false`, and the keyboard path (`view/worksheet.ts:5195`) does the same. Because `canMergeSelection()` returned true (the sheet's own budget fits), the merge button is enabled and the user's click does nothing with no explanation — exactly the failure mode `RangeOpRefusal` exists to prevent (`sheet.ts:228-239`: "the reason travels to the view so the gesture explains itself instead of looking like it did nothing"), and exactly what the task doc mandates: docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:30 — "Decide the external-paste policy explicitly, and report every refusal through the #939 notice channel (`Sheet.setOnRefusal` → `Spreadsheet.onNotice`) instead of returning in silence." No new refusal code (e.g. a `merge-budget` member) was added for this path, and `applyPasteMerges`/`moveRangeTo` likewise `continue` silently while dropping a block the user asked for.

samples.summary: YorkieStore Store-method table in the frontend design doc still describes `setMerge` as an unconditional write, though the sheets design doc was updated for the new refusing contract
samples.evidence: docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:162-171 was updated to record that `Store.setMerge` returns whether the block was stored and that the store spends its own budget, and store.ts:192-202 documents the refusal. But docs/design/frontend.md:291 — the canonical description of what YorkieStore does per Store method — still reads `| setMerge(anchor, span) | Write to root.sheets[tabId].merges[anchorSref] |`, with no mention of the budget check or the boolean refusal that is the whole point of this delta. The two design docs now give different accounts of the same method.

samples.summary: ReadOnlyStore turns the new boolean contract into a permanent refusal, so read-only sheets now lose in-memory merges the engine used to keep
samples.evidence: Every other write on `ReadOnlyStore` is a silent no-op that the engine treats as success (`setDataValidations`, `setConditionalFormats`, `setFilterState` all return void). `setMerge` now returns `false`, and the engine's three writers (sheet.ts:2730, 2977, 4929) read that as "do not record the block", so `applyPasteMerges` and `moveRangeTo` on a datasource/lakehouse tab drop merges from `Sheet.merges` that previously stayed in the in-memory model. The contract in store.ts ("refusal is not an error — the write simply did not happen") conflates "a store that persists nothing" with "a store that refused for budget"; the interface does not distinguish them, which is a fit question for the abstraction, not just this file.

samples.summary: Moving the CRDT budget check out of the `doc.update()` closure weakens the documented "floor under the CRDT": for a batch, the cap is now evaluated at queue time, not at flush
samples.evidence: The removed `applyMerge` checked the budget inside the update callback against live `root`; the new `setMerge` checks `projectedMerges()` at call time and the queued `write` closure stores unconditionally. docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:147-161 frames `YorkieStore.setMerge` as the floor under every writer of the field; between `beginBatch` and `endBatch` a remote peer's merges can land, and the flush no longer re-checks, so the stored map can end up above `MaxMergeEntries`/`MaxMergeCoveredCells`. Also note `projectedMerges` only overlays `batchMerges`, not batched `shiftCells`/`moveCells` ops that rewrite `ws.merges` wholesale.

finding.summary: Store-level merge refusal is silent — it bypasses the RangeOpRefusal/notice channel this same PR built for every other merge refusal
finding.evidence: `mergeSelection` now does `if (!(await this.store.setMerge(anchor, span))) return false;` with no `this.reportRefusal(...)`. The toolbar path (`view/spreadsheet.ts:563 toggleMergeCells`) only re-renders on `true` and shows nothing on `false`, and the keyboard path (`view/worksheet.ts:5195`) does the same. Because `canMergeSelection()` returned true (the sheet's own budget fits), the merge button is enabled and the user's click does nothing with no explanation — exactly the failure mode `RangeOpRefusal` exists to prevent (`sheet.ts:228-239`: "the reason travels to the view so the gesture explains itself instead of looking like it did nothing"), and exactly what the task doc mandates: docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:30 — "Decide the external-paste policy explicitly, and report every refusal through the #939 notice channel (`Sheet.setOnRefusal` → `Spreadsheet.onNotice`) instead of returning in silence." No new refusal code (e.g. a `merge-budget` member) was added for this path, and `applyPasteMerges`/`moveRangeTo` likewise `continue` silently while dropping a block the user asked for.

verdict.reason: The absence is real. `mergeSelection` returns false on `store.setMerge` refusal with no `this.refuse(...)` (sheet.ts:4923-4929), and the `RangeOpRefusal` union (sheet.ts:233-239) carries no member for it; all six `this.refuse` call sites (1569, 2426, 2863, 2871, 2887, 3091) are on other paths. Both view entry points drop `false` silently (view/spreadsheet.ts:563-569, view/worksheet.ts:5195-5197), and the only notice pipe is `setOnRefusal`→`refusalMessage`→`onNoticeCallback` (view/worksheet.ts:426-427), which this path never enters; the frontend toolbar ignores the return value (formatting-toolbar.tsx:257). The path is reachable with the real store: YorkieStore.setMerge returns false on budget exhaustion (yorkie-store.ts:1019-1021), and sheet.ts:4925-4928 itself documents the collaborator-drift case where `canMergeSelection` said yes. `applyPasteMerges` (2730) and `moveRangeTo` (2977) also `continue` silently. Tests codify the silence (merge.test.ts:480-534 assert no merge recorded but install no refusal listener, unlike the move/paste refusal tests at 351-392). This misses the task doc's explicit criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:30-32, "report every refusal through the #939 notice channel ... instead of returning in silence"), leaving the user's enabled merge button a no-op with no explanation — a stated outcome unmet, i.e. major under the design-fit rubric.
